verses.1:1: Love righteousness, you who judge the earth. Think of the Lord in goodness, and seek Him in simplicity of heart,
verses.1:2: for He is found by those who do not test Him, and He appears to those who have faith in Him.
verses.1:3: For crooked thoughts separate from God; and power, when tested, reproves the foolish.
verses.1:4: For wisdom will not enter a malevolent soul, nor live in a body subjected to sins.
verses.1:5: For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and will withdraw Himself from thoughts that are without understanding, and will be checked by approaching iniquity.
verses.1:6: For the Spirit of wisdom is benevolent, and will not free a blasphemer from his own lips; because God is the witness of his inward parts, and the true examiner of his heart, and the hearer of his tongue.
verses.1:7: For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the entire world, and that which holds all things together has knowledge of speech.
verses.1:8: Because of this, the one who speaks unjust things cannot remain hidden, nor will reproving judgment pass him by.
verses.1:9: For there will be an inquiry into the thoughts of the ungodly man, and the report of his words will come to God for the reproof of his iniquities.
verses.1:10: Because the ear of jealousy hears all things, and the noise of grumblings will not be concealed.
verses.1:11: Guard yourselves, therefore, from grumbling that profits nothing, and spare your tongue from slander; for a hidden word will not go in vain, and the mouth that lies kills the soul.
verses.1:12: Do not eagerly desire death in the error of your life, nor acquire destruction in the works of your hands.
verses.1:13: For God did not make death, nor does He rejoice in the destruction of the living.
verses.1:14: For He created all things so that they might exist, and He made the nations of the world healable; and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor is the kingdom of the underworld on the earth.
verses.1:15: For righteousness is perpetual and immortal.
verses.1:16: But the ungodly with hands and words summoned it, and considering it a friend, they wasted away; and they made pledges with it, because they are worthy to be on its side.
verses.2:1: For they said, thinking wrongly within themselves: "The time of our life is short and accompanied by weariness, and there is no relief at a man's end, and there is no one who has been known to have returned from the underworld.
verses.2:2: Because we were born out of nothing, and after this we will be as though we had not been. For the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and speech is a spark to stir our heart;
verses.2:3: when it is extinguished, our body will be ashes, and the spirit will disperse like soft air; and our life will pass away like the trace of a cloud, and will dissolve like a mist that has been driven off by the rays of the sun and weighed down by its heat.
verses.2:4: And our name will fall into oblivion over time, and no one will hold remembrance of our works.
verses.2:5: For our time is the passing of a shadow, and there is no return of our end; because it has been sealed, and no one returns.
verses.2:6: Come, therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that exist, and let us make use of creation swiftly, as in youth.
verses.2:7: Let us fill ourselves with precious wine and perfumes, and let the flower of the season not pass us by.
verses.2:8: Let us crown ourselves with roses before they wither; let there be no meadow that our revelry does not pass through;
verses.2:9: let none of us be without a part in our revelry. Everywhere let us leave signs of gladness, because this is our share, and this is our lot.
verses.2:10: Let us oppress the righteous poor man, and let us not spare the widow, nor revere the gray hairs of the old man of long years;
verses.2:11: rather, let our strength be the law of righteousness; for what is weak is found to be useless.
verses.2:12: Let us ensnare the righteous man, therefore, because he is useless to us, and is opposed to our works, and reproaches us for sins against the law, and spreads abroad against us sins against our discipline.
verses.2:13: He professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a son of God.
verses.2:14: He has become to us an exposure of our thoughts.
verses.2:15: He is burdensome to us even to look at, because his life is unlike that of others, and his ways are altered.
verses.2:16: We have been considered by him as triflers, and he keeps himself away from our ways as from impurities, and he prefers the final end of the righteous, and he boasts that he has God as Father.
verses.2:17: Let us see, therefore, whether his words are true, and let us test what is going to come to him, and we will know what his final end will be.
verses.2:18: For if he is a true son of God, He will uphold him and deliver him from the hands of adversaries.
verses.2:19: Let us examine him with insult and torment, so that we may know his reverence and test his patience.
verses.2:20: Let us condemn him to a most shameful death; for there will be regard for him according to his words."
verses.2:21: These things they thought, and they went astray; for their malice blinded them.
verses.2:22: And they did not know the mysteries of God, nor did they hope for the reward of righteousness, nor did they discern the honor of holy souls.
verses.2:23: For God created man indestructible, and made him in the image of His own likeness.
verses.2:24: But through the envy of the devil death entered the world, and those who are on his side imitate him.
verses.3:1: But the souls of the righteous are in God's hand, and the torment of death will not touch them.
verses.3:2: In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure was regarded as affliction,
verses.3:3: and their journey away from us as destruction; but they are in peace;
verses.3:4: even though before men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality.
verses.3:5: In a few things they were afflicted, in many things they will be well provided for, because God tested them and found them worthy of Himself.
verses.3:6: Like gold in the furnace He proved them, and like the sacrifice of a burnt offering He accepted them, and in time there will be regard for them.
verses.3:7: The righteous will shine, and like sparks in a reed bed they will dart about.
verses.3:8: They will judge nations and hold dominion over peoples, and their Lord will reign forever.
verses.3:9: Those who trust in Him will understand the truth, and those who are faithful in love will find rest in Him, because gift and peace belong to His chosen ones.
verses.3:10: But the ungodly will receive chastisement according to what they thought: those who disregarded the righteous man and departed from the Lord.
verses.3:11: For the one who casts aside wisdom and discipline is wretched; and their hope is empty, their labors without fruit, and their works useless.
verses.3:12: Their wives are senseless, and their children are most wicked.
verses.3:13: Cursed is their offspring, because the barren woman is blessed; and the undefiled woman, who has not known a bed in transgression, will have fruit in the visitation of holy souls;
verses.3:14: and the eunuch who has not worked iniquity through his hands, nor thought most wicked things against God; for a chosen gift of faith will be given to him, and a most acceptable lot in the temple of God.
verses.3:15: For glorious is the fruit of good labors, and the root of wisdom cannot fail.
verses.3:16: But the children of adulterers will remain incomplete, and the seed from an unlawful bed will be destroyed.
verses.3:17: And if indeed they have a long life, they will be counted as nothing, and their final old age will be without honor;
verses.3:18: and if they die sooner, they will have no hope, nor consolation in the day of recognition.
verses.3:19: For the endings of an unjust nation are dire.
verses.4:1: Oh, how beautiful is a chaste generation with splendor! For its memory is immortal, since it is known both before God and before people.
verses.4:2: When it is present, they imitate it, and they long for it when it has withdrawn; and crowned forever, it triumphs, winning the prize of undefiled contests.
verses.4:3: But the prolific multitude of the wicked will not be useful, and illegitimate shoots will not put down deep roots, nor will they establish a stable foundation.
verses.4:4: Even if they sprout in branches for a time, being weakly set, they will be shaken by the wind, and by the violence of the winds they will be uprooted.
verses.4:5: For the unperfected branches will be broken; and their fruits are useless and sour to eat, and fit for nothing.
verses.4:6: For the children who are born from unlawful sleeps are witnesses of wickedness against their parents in their examination.
verses.4:7: But if the righteous man is overtaken early by death, he will be in refreshment;
verses.4:8: for honorable old age is not one of long duration, nor reckoned by the number of years; rather, gray hair is a person's understanding,
verses.4:9: and the age of old age is an unblemished life.
verses.4:10: Pleasing God, he became beloved, and while living among sinners, he was carried away.
verses.4:11: He was snatched away so that malice would not alter his mind, or falsehood deceive his soul.
verses.4:12: For the bewitchment of frivolity obscures good things, and the instability of desire overturns a mind without malice.
verses.4:13: Perfected in a short time, he fulfilled long periods of time;
verses.4:14: for his soul was pleasing to God; for this reason He hurried to bring him out from the midst of iniquities. Yet the peoples saw and did not understand, nor did they lay such things to heart,
verses.4:15: that the grace of God and mercy are toward His holy ones, and regard is toward His chosen ones.
verses.4:16: Moreover, the righteous man who has died condemns the living wicked, and youth swiftly perfected condemns the long life of the unrighteous.
verses.4:17: For they will see the end of the wise man, and they will not understand what God purposed concerning him, and why the Lord safeguarded him.
verses.4:18: They will see and despise him; but the Lord will mock them.
verses.4:19: And after these things they will fall down without honor, and be in disgrace among the dead forever; because He will burst them open, puffed up without a voice, and He will shake them from their foundations, and they will be laid waste to the uttermost, and they will be groaning, and their memory will perish.
verses.4:20: They will come fearful in the thought of their sins, and their own iniquities will expose them to their face.
verses.5:1: Then the righteous will stand in great steadfastness against those who distressed them and who took away their labors.
verses.5:2: Seeing this, they will be troubled with dreadful fear, and they will be amazed at the suddenness of unexpected salvation,
verses.5:3: saying within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit: "These are the ones whom we once held in derision and as a byword of reproach.
verses.5:4: We senseless ones regarded their life as madness, and their end as without honor;
verses.5:5: look how they have been reckoned among the sons of God, and their lot is among the holy ones.
verses.5:6: Therefore we have strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shone on us, and the sun of understanding has not risen for us.
verses.5:7: We grew weary in the way of iniquity and destruction, and we walked difficult ways; but we did not know the way of the Lord.
verses.5:8: What did pride profit us? Or what did the boasting of riches bring us?
verses.5:9: All those things have passed away like a shadow, and like a messenger hurrying past,
verses.5:10: and like a ship that passes through surging water, of which, when it has passed by, no trace can be found, nor the track of its keel in the waves;
verses.5:11: or like a bird that flies across in the air, of whose course no proof is found, but only the sound of wings beating the light wind and splitting the air by the force of its course: with its wings set in motion, it flew across, and after this no sign of its course is found;
verses.5:12: or like an arrow shot toward a designated place, the divided air immediately closed back into itself, so that its passage is unknown:
verses.5:13: so we too, once born, immediately ceased to be; and indeed we were able to show no sign of virtue, but in our wickedness we were consumed." Such things those who sinned spoke in the underworld,
verses.5:14: because the hope of the wicked man is like thistledown that is carried off by the wind, and like thin foam that is scattered by a storm, and like smoke that is dispersed by the wind, and like the memory of a guest of one day passing by.
verses.5:15: But the righteous will live forever, and their reward is with the Lord, and thought for them is with the Most High.
verses.5:16: Therefore they will receive a kingdom of splendor and a diadem of beauty from the hand of the Lord; because with His right hand He will shelter them, and with His holy arm He will defend them.
verses.5:17: His zeal will take up armor and arm creation for vengeance upon enemies.
verses.5:18: He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and He will take certain judgment as a helmet;
verses.5:19: He will take up equity as an unconquerable shield.
verses.5:20: And He will sharpen harsh wrath into a spear, and the whole world will fight with Him against the senseless.
verses.5:21: Bolts of lightning will go straight, and as from a well-bent bow of the clouds they will be driven forth, and they will leap to a fixed place.
verses.5:22: And from stony wrath, full hailstones will be sent; the water of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will rush together harshly.
verses.5:23: A spirit of might will stand against them, and like a tempest of wind it will divide them; and their iniquity will bring the whole earth to a wasteland, and wickedness will overturn the thrones of the mighty.
verses.6:1: Wisdom is better than strength, and a prudent man than a strong one. Listen, therefore, kings, and understand; learn, judges of the ends of the earth.
verses.6:2: Give ear, you who govern multitudes and are pleased with yourselves over crowds of nations.
verses.6:3: For power was given to you by the Lord, and might by the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your thoughts.
verses.6:4: Because while you were ministers of His kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor did you keep the law of righteousness, nor did you walk according to the will of God.
verses.6:5: Dreadfully and swiftly He will appear to you, because the harshest judgment will come upon those who rule.
verses.6:6: For mercy is granted to the lowly; but the mighty will mightily suffer torments.
verses.6:7: For God will not exempt anyone's person, nor will He stand in awe of anyone's greatness, because He Himself made the small and the great, and He has equal care for all.
verses.6:8: But for the stronger, a stronger torment is at hand.
verses.6:9: To you, therefore, kings, are these words of mine, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.
verses.6:10: For those who have kept just things justly will be justified, and those who have learned these things will find what to answer.
verses.6:11: Desire my words, therefore; love them, and you will have discipline.
verses.6:12: Radiant is wisdom, and she never fades; and she is easily seen by those who love her, and found by those who seek her.
verses.6:13: She anticipates those who desire her, so that she may show herself to them first.
verses.6:14: Whoever wakes at daybreak for her will not toil; for he will find her sitting beside his doors.
verses.6:15: Therefore to think upon her is perfected understanding, and whoever keeps watch on account of her will swiftly be free from care.
verses.6:16: For she herself goes about seeking those worthy of her, and along the paths she shows herself cheerfully, and in every providence she meets them.
verses.6:17: For her beginning is the truest desire for discipline.
verses.6:18: Therefore care for discipline is love, and love is the keeping of her laws; and the observance of laws is the perfection of incorruption;
verses.6:19: and incorruption makes one near to God.
verses.6:20: Desire for wisdom, therefore, leads to an everlasting kingdom.
verses.6:21: If, therefore, you delight in thrones and scepters, kings of the people, love wisdom, so that you may reign forever; love the light of wisdom, all you who rule over peoples.
verses.6:22: Now what wisdom is, and how she came to be, I will declare, and I will not hide the mysteries of God from you; but I will investigate from the beginning of her birth, and I will set the knowledge of her in the light, and I will not pass by the truth.
verses.6:23: Neither will I journey with wasting envy, because such a person will not be a partaker of wisdom.
verses.6:24: Now a multitude of the wise is the health of the whole world, and a wise king is the stability of the people.
verses.6:25: Therefore receive discipline through my words, and it will profit you.
verses.7:1: Indeed, I too am a mortal man, like everyone else, and of the lineage of that earthly one who was made first; and in a mother's womb I was shaped as flesh;
verses.7:2: in the space of ten months I was congealed in blood, from the seed of a man and the accompanying delight of sleep.
verses.7:3: And when I was born, I received the common air, and fell upon the similarly made earth, and weeping, I uttered a first cry like everyone else.
verses.7:4: In swaddling cloths I was nurtured, and with great cares;
verses.7:5: for no one among kings had a different beginning of birth.
verses.7:6: Therefore there is one entrance into life for all, and a like departure.
verses.7:7: For this reason I wished, and understanding was given to me; and I called out, and the spirit of wisdom came into me;
verses.7:8: and I preferred her to kingdoms and thrones, and I reckoned riches to be nothing in comparison with her.
verses.7:9: Nor did I compare a precious stone to her, because all gold in comparison with her is a little sand, and silver will be counted as mud in her sight.
verses.7:10: Above health and beauty I loved her, and I resolved to have her in place of light, because her light is unquenchable.
verses.7:11: Now all good things came to me together with her, and wealth beyond number through her hands;
verses.7:12: and I rejoiced in them all, because this wisdom went before me, and I did not know that she is the mother of all these things.
verses.7:13: Without pretense I learned her, and without envy I share her, and I do not hide her wealth.
verses.7:14: For she is a boundless treasure for men; those who have made use of it have become sharers in the friendship of God, commended because of the gifts of instruction.
verses.7:15: Now God has granted me to speak with judgment, and to conceive things worthy of those things that are given to me, because He Himself is the guide of wisdom and the corrector of the wise.
verses.7:16: For in His hand are both we and our words, and all wisdom, and knowledge of works, and instruction.
verses.7:17: For He Himself gave me true knowledge of the things that exist, so that I might know the arrangement of the world and the powers of the elements,
verses.7:18: the beginning and the end and the middle of times, the shifts of alternations and the changes of seasons,
verses.7:19: the courses of the year and the arrangements of the stars,
verses.7:20: the natures of animals and the rages of wild beasts, the force of winds and the thoughts of men, the differences of shrubs and the powers of roots.
verses.7:21: And whatever things are hidden and unforeseen I learned, for wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me.
verses.7:22: For there is in her a spirit of understanding, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, eloquent, mobile, undefiled, clear, sweet, loving the good, keen, which nothing hinders, doing good,
verses.7:23: humane, gracious, firm, certain, untroubled, possessing all power, watching over all things, and which encompasses all spirits; intelligent, pure, subtle.
verses.7:24: For wisdom is more mobile than all moving things, and she reaches everywhere because of her purity.
verses.7:25: For she is a vapor of God's power, and a certain pure outflow of the splendor of almighty God; and therefore nothing defiled enters into her.
verses.7:26: For she is the radiance of eternal light, and a mirror without blemish of the majesty of God, and an image of His goodness.
verses.7:27: And though she is one, she can do all things; and remaining in herself, she renews all things; and through the nations she passes into holy souls; she appoints friends of God and prophets.
verses.7:28: For God loves no one except the one who dwells with wisdom.
verses.7:29: For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above every arrangement of the stars; compared with light, she is found superior.
verses.7:30: For night succeeds it, but malice does not overcome wisdom.
verses.8:1: Therefore she reaches from end to end strongly, and she arranges all things sweetly.
verses.8:2: I loved her and sought her out from my youth, and I sought to take her to myself as a bride, and I became a lover of her beauty.
verses.8:3: She glorifies her noble birth, having companionship with God; and indeed, the Lord of all loved her.
verses.8:4: For she is the teacher of the instruction of God, and the chooser of His works.
verses.8:5: And if riches are desired in life, what is richer than wisdom, who works all things?
verses.8:6: And if understanding works, who more than she is the artisan of the things that exist?
verses.8:7: And if anyone loves justice, her labors have great virtues: for she teaches sobriety and prudence, and justice and fortitude; nothing in life is more useful to men than these.
verses.8:8: And if anyone desires an abundance of knowledge, she knows past things and judges concerning future things; she knows the subtleties of words and the solutions of arguments; she knows signs and portents before they happen, and the outcomes of times and ages.
verses.8:9: Therefore I resolved to bring her to myself to live with me, knowing that she will share with me in good things, and will be a consolation for my thought and my weariness.
verses.8:10: Because of her I will have renown before the crowds, and honor among the elders as a young man;
verses.8:11: and I will be found keen in judgment, and in the sight of the mighty I will be admirable, and the faces of princes will marvel at me.
verses.8:12: When I am silent they will wait for me, and when I speak they will look to me, and when I discourse at greater length they will place their hands upon their mouth.
verses.8:13: Furthermore, through her I will have immortality, and I will leave an eternal memory to those who will come after me.
verses.8:14: I will govern peoples, and nations will be subject to me;
verses.8:15: terrifying kings will fear me when they hear of me. Among the multitude I will appear good, and in war strong.
verses.8:16: Entering into my house, I will rest with her; for her company has no bitterness, nor does shared life with her have weariness, but gladness and joy.
verses.8:17: Pondering these things within myself and reflecting in my heart that immortality is in kinship with wisdom,
verses.8:18: and in her friendship is good delight, and in the works of her hands is wealth without failing, and in the contest of her conversation is wisdom, and high renown in the sharing of her words: I went about seeking that I might take her to myself.
verses.8:19: Now I was a gifted boy, and I received a good soul as my lot.
verses.8:20: And since I was even more good, I came to an undefiled body.
verses.8:21: And when I knew that I could not otherwise be self-controlled unless God gives it, and that this very thing belonged to wisdom, to know whose gift this was, I approached the Lord and implored Him, and I spoke from my whole heart:
verses.9:1: "God of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who made all things by Your word,
verses.9:2: and by Your wisdom established man, so that he might rule over the creation that was made by You,
verses.9:3: that he might govern the world in equity and justice, and in uprightness of heart render judgment:
verses.9:4: give me wisdom, who sits beside Your thrones, and do not reject me from among Your children;
verses.9:5: for I am Your servant and the son of Your maidservant, a weak man and of short time, and too little for the understanding of judgment and laws.
verses.9:6: For even if anyone is perfected among the sons of men, if Your wisdom is absent from him, he will be counted as nothing.
verses.9:7: You chose me as king for Your people, and as judge of Your sons and daughters;
verses.9:8: and You told me to build a temple on Your holy mountain, and an altar in the city of Your dwelling, a likeness of Your holy tabernacle, which You prepared from the beginning.
verses.9:9: And with You is Your wisdom, who knows Your works, and who was also present then when You made the world, and knew what was pleasing to Your eyes and what was upright in Your commandments.
verses.9:10: Send her from Your holy heavens, and from the throne of Your greatness, so that she may be with me and labor with me, so that I may know what is acceptable before You;
verses.9:11: for she knows all things and understands, and she will guide me soberly in my works, and will guard me in her power.
verses.9:12: And my works will be acceptable, and I will govern Your people justly, and I will be worthy of the thrones of my father.
verses.9:13: For who among men will be able to know the counsel of God? Or who will be able to conceive what God wills?
verses.9:14: For the thoughts of mortals are timid, and our foresights are uncertain;
verses.9:15: for the body that decays burdens the soul, and the earthly dwelling weighs down the mind that ponders many things.
verses.9:16: And with difficulty we estimate the things that are on earth, and with labor we find the things that are in view; but who will search out the things that are in the heavens?
verses.9:17: And who will know Your mind, unless You give wisdom and send Your Holy Spirit from the highest places,
verses.9:18: and thus the paths of those who are on earth are set straight, and men learn the things that please You? For through wisdom all who pleased You, Lord, from the beginning were healed."
verses.10:1: She guarded the one who was first formed by God, the Father of the world, when he was created alone,
verses.10:2: and brought him out of his transgression, and gave him strength to control all things.
verses.10:3: When an unrighteous man withdrew from her in his anger, he perished through the anger of murdering his brother.
verses.10:4: Because of him, when water was destroying the earth, wisdom healed it again, steering the righteous man by a paltry piece of wood.
verses.10:5: She also, when the nations had gathered together in an agreement of wickedness, knew the righteous man, and preserved him blameless before God, and kept him strong amid compassion for his son.
verses.10:6: She delivered the righteous man as he fled from the perishing ungodly, while fire came down upon Pentapolis.
verses.10:7: As a witness to their wickedness, a smoking deserted land still remains, and trees bearing fruit at an uncertain time, and a standing figure of salt, a memorial of an unbelieving soul.
verses.10:8: For in passing by wisdom, they not only fell into this, that they were ignorant of what is good, but also left mankind a memorial of their folly, so that in the things in which they sinned they could not even remain hidden.
verses.10:9: But wisdom delivered those who attend to her from sorrows.
verses.10:10: She led the righteous man fleeing his brother's anger along straight paths, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him knowledge of holy things; she honored him in his labors and brought his labors to completion.
verses.10:11: In the deceit of those defrauding him she stood by him, and made him honorable.
verses.10:12: She guarded him from enemies, and protected him from deceivers; and she gave him a fierce struggle so that he might prevail and know that wisdom is more powerful than all.
verses.10:13: She did not abandon the righteous man when he was sold, but delivered him from sinners; and she went down with him into the pit,
verses.10:14: and in chains she did not abandon him, until she brought him the scepter of a kingdom and power against those who oppressed him; and she showed those who sullied him to be liars, and gave him eternal glory.
verses.10:15: She delivered a righteous people and a blameless offspring from the nations that oppressed them.
verses.10:16: She entered into the soul of the servant of God, and stood against terrifying kings with wonders and signs.
verses.10:17: And she rendered to the righteous the reward of their labors, and led them along a wondrous way; and she became for them a covering by day, and a light of stars through the night;
verses.10:18: she brought them across through the Red Sea, and carried them across through vast water.
verses.10:19: But their enemies she sank into the sea, and from the depth of the underworld she brought them up. Therefore the righteous carried off the spoils of the ungodly,
verses.10:20: and they sang praises to Your holy name, Lord, and praised Your victorious hand together,
verses.10:21: because wisdom opened the mouth of the mute, and made the tongues of infants articulate.
verses.11:1: She directed their works by the hands of a holy prophet.
verses.11:2: They journeyed through deserts that were not inhabited, and in deserted places they set up huts.
verses.11:3: They stood against foes, and avenged themselves on their enemies.
verses.11:4: They thirsted and called upon You, and water was given to them from a very high rock, and relief from thirst from hard stone.
verses.11:5: For through the things by which their enemies suffered punishment from the lack of their drink, and in which the sons of Israel rejoiced when they had abundance, through these same things, when they lacked them, they were treated well.
verses.11:6: For indeed, in place of the spring of an ever-flowing river, You gave human blood to the unrighteous.
verses.11:7: While they were diminished in the reproof of the killed infants, You gave them abundant water unexpectedly,
verses.11:8: showing through the thirst that occurred then how You exalted Your own and put their adversaries to death.
verses.11:9: For when they were tested, though indeed receiving discipline with mercy, they knew how the ungodly, judged with anger, suffered torments.
verses.11:10: These indeed You tried like a father who admonishes; but those You condemned like a harsh king who interrogates.
verses.11:11: For both absent and present, they were tormented alike.
verses.11:12: For a double weariness and groaning had seized them, along with the memory of past things.
verses.11:13: For when they heard that through their own torments they were being treated well, they remembered the Lord, marveling at the end of the outcome.
verses.11:14: For the one whom they mocked when he was cast out in wicked exposure, they admired at the end of the result, not thirsting in the same way as the righteous.
verses.11:15: But in return for the senseless thoughts of their iniquity, because some, going astray, worshiped mute serpents and worthless beasts, You sent upon them a multitude of mute animals for vengeance,
verses.11:16: so that they might know that through the things by which one sins, through these one is also tormented.
verses.11:17: For Your almighty hand, which created the world out of unseen matter, was not unable to send upon them a multitude of bears or bold lions,
verses.11:18: or unknown beasts of a new kind, full of anger, either breathing a vapor of fires, or putting forth an odor of smoke, or shooting terrifying sparks from their eyes.
verses.11:19: Not only could an injury from these exterminate them, but even the sight of these could kill through fear.
verses.11:20: Yet even without these they could have been killed by a single breath, pursued by their very own deeds and scattered by the breath of Your power; but You have set all things in order by measure, number, and weight.
verses.11:21: For great strength has always remained with You alone; and who will resist the power of Your arm?
verses.11:22: Because like the tipping of a scale, so is the world before You, and like a drop of pre-dawn dew that comes down upon the earth.
verses.11:23: Yet You show mercy to all, because You are able to do all things; and You overlook the sins of mankind on account of repentance.
verses.11:24: For You love all that exists, and You hate nothing of the things You have made; for You neither established nor made anything while hating it.
verses.11:25: And how could anything endure unless You had willed it? Or how could that which had not been called by You be preserved?
verses.11:26: Yet You spare all things, because they are Yours, Lord, You who love souls.
verses.12:1: Oh, how good and sweet is Your Spirit in all things, Lord!
verses.12:2: Therefore, by degrees You reprove those who go astray, and concerning the things in which they sin You warn and speak to them, so that, having abandoned wickedness, they may believe in You, Lord.
verses.12:3: For those ancient inhabitants of Your holy land, whom You abhorred,
verses.12:4: because they performed works hateful to You through sorceries and unrighteous sacrifices,
verses.12:5: and killers of their own children without mercy, and eaters of human entrails, and devourers of blood from the midst of Your mystery,
verses.12:6: and parents, authors of helpless souls, You willed to destroy by the hands of our ancestors,
verses.12:7: so that they might receive a worthy sojourn of the children of God, which is the land dearer to You than all.
verses.12:8: Yet You spared even these as human beings, and sent wasps as forerunners of Your army, so that they might gradually exterminate them.
verses.12:9: Not because You were powerless to subject the ungodly to the righteous in war, or to exterminate them all at once by fierce beasts or by a harsh word,
verses.12:10: but judging by degrees, You gave room for repentance, not unaware that their nation is evil and their wickedness is natural, and that their thinking could not be changed for all time.
verses.12:11: For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; and it was not out of fear of anyone that You granted pardon for their sins.
verses.12:12: For who will say to You, "What have You done?" Or who will stand against Your judgment? Or who will come into Your presence as an avenger of wicked people? Or who will hold it against You if the nations that You made perish?
verses.12:13: For there is no other god besides You, whose care is for all things, so that You should show that You do not render judgment unrighteously.
verses.12:14: Neither king nor tyrant will inquire in Your presence concerning those whom You have destroyed.
verses.12:15: Since You are righteous, then, You govern all things righteously; You consider it alien to Your power to condemn even the one who ought not to be punished.
verses.12:16: For Your power is the beginning of righteousness, and because You are the Lord, You make Yourself spare all.
verses.12:17: For You show power, You who are not believed to be complete in power, and You expose the audacity of those who do not know You.
verses.12:18: But You, sovereign of power, judge with tranquility and govern us with great reverence; for the ability is at Your disposal whenever You will.
verses.12:19: And You taught Your people through such works that one ought to be righteous and humane, and You made Your sons full of good hope, because in judging You give room for repentance in sins.
verses.12:20: For if You tormented with such great attentiveness those who were enemies of Your servants and due for death, giving time and place through which they might be changed from wickedness,
verses.12:21: with how great diligence You judged Your sons, to whose ancestors You gave oaths and covenants of good promises!
verses.12:22: Therefore, when You give us discipline, You scourge our enemies many times over, so that when we judge we may think on Your goodness, and when we are judged we may hope for Your mercy.
verses.12:23: For this reason also, to those who lived senselessly and unrighteously in their life, You gave the utmost torments through the things that they worshiped.
verses.12:24: For indeed, they strayed too long on the way of error, considering as gods those things that among animals are worthless, living in the manner of senseless infants.
verses.12:25: Because of this, as to senseless children, You gave judgment in derision.
verses.12:26: But those who were not corrected by mockeries and rebukes experienced a judgment worthy of God.
verses.12:27: For in the things in which they grew indignant while suffering through these whom they thought to be gods, seeing as they were being exterminated by those very ones, they recognized as the true God Him whom they once denied knowing; on account of which the end of their condemnation also came upon them.
verses.13:1: Now all people are foolish in whom the knowledge of God is not present; and from these good things that are seen, they could not understand Him who is, nor, paying attention to the works, did they recognize who the craftsman was;
verses.13:2: but either fire, or wind, or swift air, or the circle of the stars, or immense water, or the sun and the moon, they thought to be gods, rulers of the world.
verses.13:3: If, delighted by their beauty, they thought them to be gods, let them know how much more beautiful than these their sovereign is; for the originator of beauty established all these things.
verses.13:4: Or if they marveled at their power and works, let them understand from them that He who made these things is stronger than they;
verses.13:5: for from the greatness of beauty and of creation, the Creator of these things will be able to be recognizably seen.
verses.13:6: Yet still, concerning these there is less complaint; for even these perhaps go astray while seeking God and wishing to find Him.
verses.13:7: For indeed, while they go about among His works, they inquire, and they are persuaded that the things that are seen are good.
verses.13:8: Again, however, not even these ought to be excused.
verses.13:9: For if they were able to know so much that they could estimate the world, how did they not more easily find the Lord of it?
verses.13:10: But wretched are they, and their hope is among the dead, who called the works of human hands gods: gold and silver, the invention of craft, and likenesses of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
verses.13:11: Or if some skilled carpenter cuts a straight piece of wood from the forest, and skillfully scrapes off all its bark, and, using his craft, diligently fashions a vessel useful for the conduct of life;
verses.13:12: and uses up the remnants of that work for the preparation of food,
verses.13:13: and the remnant of these that serves no use, a crooked piece of wood and full of knots, he carves diligently in his leisure, and through the knowledge of his craft shapes it, and likens it to the image of a human being,
verses.13:14: or compares it to one of the animals, coating it with red ocher, and making its color ruddy with dye, and coating over every blemish that is in it;
verses.13:15: and makes for it a worthy dwelling, both placing it on the wall and securing it with iron
verses.13:16: so that it may not happen to fall, watching out for it, knowing that it cannot help itself; for it is an image, and it has need of help.
verses.13:17: And concerning his possessions, and his children, and marriage, making a vow he inquires; he is not ashamed to speak with one who is without life.
verses.13:18: And indeed for health he pleads with one who is weak, and for life he begs one who is dead, and for help he calls upon one who is useless.
verses.13:19: And for a journey he asks of one who cannot walk; and concerning acquiring, and working, and the outcome of all things, he asks of one who is useless in all things.
verses.14:1: Again, another, planning to sail and beginning to make a journey through fierce waves, calls upon a piece of wood more fragile than the wood carrying him.
verses.14:2: For the desire for gain devised that, and the craftsman built it by his wisdom.
verses.14:3: Yet Your providence, Father, steers it, because You have given a way even in the sea, and a most secure path among the waves,
verses.14:4: showing that You are able to save from all things, even if someone goes to the sea without skill.
verses.14:5: Yet so that the works of Your wisdom would not be empty, for this reason people entrust their lives even to a small piece of wood, and crossing the sea by a raft, they have been delivered.
verses.14:6: Moreover, even from the beginning, when the proud giants were perishing, the hope of the world, fleeing for refuge to a raft, left to the age the seed of generation, which was steered by Your hand.
verses.14:7: For blessed is the wood through which righteousness comes about;
verses.14:8: but the idol that is made by hands is cursed, both itself and the one who made it, because the one indeed did the work, while the other, though it was fragile, was named a god.
verses.14:9: And equally hateful to God are the ungodly person and his ungodliness;
verses.14:10: for indeed what was made will suffer torments along with the one who made it.
verses.14:11: For this reason there will be no regard even for the idols of the nations, because the creatures of God have become an object of hatred, and a temptation for the souls of people, and a trap for the feet of the foolish.
verses.14:12: For the beginning of fornication is the devising of idols, and their invention is the corruption of life:
verses.14:13: for neither did they exist from the beginning, nor will they exist forever.
verses.14:14: For this futility of people came into the world, and therefore a brief end for them has been found.
verses.14:15: For a father, grieving with bitter mourning, made an image of the son quickly snatched away from him; and the one who then had died as a man he now began to worship as a god, and he established sacred rites and sacrifices among his servants.
verses.14:16: Then, as time passed and the wicked custom grew strong, this error was kept as a law, and by the command of tyrants fashioned images were worshiped.
verses.14:17: And as for those whom people could not honor openly because they were far away, with their likeness brought from afar, they made a visible image of the king whom they wanted to honor, so that by their eagerness they might worship the one who was absent as though present.
verses.14:18: Moreover, the extraordinary diligence of the craftsman led even those who were ignorant to the worship of these.
verses.14:19: For he, wishing to please the one who engaged him, labored with his skill to shape the likeness for the better.
verses.14:20: And the multitude of people, carried away by the beauty of the work, now considered the one who earlier had been honored as a man to be a god.
verses.14:21: And this was the deception of human life, because people, serving either affection or kings, placed the incommunicable name upon stones and pieces of wood.
verses.14:22: And it had not been enough for them to have erred concerning the knowledge of God, but living also in a great war of ignorance, they call so many and such great evils peace.
verses.14:23: For either sacrificing their children, or offering secret sacrifices, or holding vigils full of madness,
verses.14:24: they no longer keep either life or marriage pure, but one kills another out of envy, or grieves him by committing adultery,
verses.14:25: and all things are mixed together: blood, murder, theft and deceit, corruption and faithlessness, turmoil and perjury, disturbance of the good,
verses.14:26: forgetfulness of God, defilement of souls, alteration of birth, instability of marriage, disorder of adultery and shamelessness.
verses.14:27: For the worship of unspeakable idols is the cause of every evil, both the beginning and the end.
verses.14:28: For either while rejoicing they go mad, or surely they prophesy falsehoods, or they live unrighteously, or they quickly commit perjury.
verses.14:29: For while they trust in idols that are without a soul, swearing wickedly, they do not expect to be harmed.
verses.14:30: Therefore both will deservedly come upon them, because they thought wickedly about God, giving heed to idols, and swore unrighteously, despising righteousness in deceit.
verses.14:31: For it is not the power of the things sworn by, but the punishment of sinners, that always pursues the transgression of the unrighteous.
verses.15:1: But You, our God, are kind and true, patient, and ordering all things in mercy.
verses.15:2: For even if we sin, we are Yours, knowing Your greatness; and if we do not sin, we know that we are counted with You.
verses.15:3: For to know You is complete righteousness; and to know Your righteousness and power is the root of immortality.
verses.15:4: For the devising of people's evil craft has not led us into error, nor the shadow of a painting, a labor without fruit, a figure carved in various colors,
verses.15:5: the sight of which gives desire to the senseless person, and he loves the figure of a dead image without a soul.
verses.15:6: Lovers of evil things are worthy to have hope in such things, both those who make them, and those who love them, and those who worship them.
verses.15:7: Moreover, a potter, pressing soft earth, laboriously fashions each vessel for our uses; and from the same clay he fashions vessels that are clean for use, and likewise those that are contrary to these; yet the potter is the judge of what the use of these vessels is.
verses.15:8: And with vain labor he who a little while before had been made from the earth fashions a god from the same clay, and after a little while returns to the place from which he was taken, when the debt of the soul that he had is demanded back from him.
verses.15:9: Yet his concern is not that he is about to toil, nor that his life is short; rather, he competes with goldsmiths and silversmiths, and he even imitates coppersmiths, and he claims glory because he fashions useless things.
verses.15:10: For his heart is ashes, and his hope is useless earth, and his life is more worthless than clay,
verses.15:11: because he did not know Him who fashioned him, and who breathed into him a soul that works, and who blew into him a living spirit.
verses.15:12: Moreover, they considered that our life is a game, and the conduct of life is arranged for profit, and that one must make gain from any source, even from evil.
verses.15:13: For this man knows that he sins above all others, who from the material of the earth fashions fragile vessels and carved images.
verses.15:14: For all the enemies of Your people, and those who rule over them, are foolish, and wretched beyond measure, proud of soul,
verses.15:15: because they considered all the idols of the nations to be gods, which have neither the use of eyes for seeing, nor nostrils for drawing breath, nor ears for hearing, nor fingers of hands for handling, and even their feet are sluggish for walking.
verses.15:16: For a human being made them, and he who borrowed breath fashioned them. For no human being will be able to fashion a god like himself.
verses.15:17: For since he is mortal, he fashions a dead thing with wicked hands. For he himself is better than those whom he worships, because he indeed lived, though he was mortal, whereas they never did.
verses.15:18: Moreover, they worship even the most wretched animals; for, being senseless, compared with these, they are worse than those.
verses.15:19: Yet not even in appearance can anyone perceive good things in these animals; rather, they have escaped the praise of God and His blessing.
verses.16:1: Because of these things, they also deservedly suffered torments through things similar to these, and through a multitude of beasts they were destroyed.
verses.16:2: Instead of these torments, You treated Your people well, to whom You gave the desire of their delight, a new taste, preparing quail for them as food,
verses.16:3: so that those indeed, desiring food, because of the things that were shown and sent to them might be turned away even from necessary desire. These, however, having become needy for a short time, tasted a new food.
verses.16:4: For it was necessary indeed for destruction without excuse to come upon those exercising tyranny, yet only to show to these how their enemies were being destroyed.
verses.16:5: For indeed, when the fierce wrath of beasts came upon them, they were being destroyed by the bites of crooked serpents.
verses.16:6: But Your wrath did not remain forever; rather, for correction they were troubled for a short time, having a sign of salvation as a reminder of the commandment of Your law.
verses.16:7: For the one who turned was not healed through what he saw, but through You, the Savior of all.
verses.16:8: And in this You showed our enemies that it is You who deliver from every evil.
verses.16:9: For the bites of locusts and flies killed them, and no healing was found for their soul, because they were worthy to be destroyed by such things.
verses.16:10: Yet not even the teeth of venomous dragons overcame Your children, for Your mercy came and healed them.
verses.16:11: For in the remembrance of Your words they were examined and quickly saved, so that, falling into deep forgetfulness, they might not be unable to make use of Your help.
verses.16:12: For indeed neither herb nor poultice healed them, but Your word, Lord, which heals all things.
verses.16:13: For it is You, Lord, who have authority over life and death, and lead down to the gates of death, and bring back.
verses.16:14: A man, however, indeed kills through malice; and when the spirit has gone out, it will not return, nor will he call back the soul that has been received.
verses.16:15: But it is impossible to escape Your hand.
verses.16:16: For the ungodly, denying that they knew You, were scourged by the strength of Your arm, suffering persecution by unusual waters and hailstorms and rains, and consumed by fire.
verses.16:17: For, what was marvelous, in water, which extinguishes all things, fire prevailed even more; for the world is the defender of the righteous.
verses.16:18: For at one time the fire was tamed, so that the animals that had been sent to the ungodly would not be burned up, but so that they themselves, upon seeing, might know that they are suffering persecution by the judgment of God.
verses.16:19: And at another time, in water, fire blazed up on every side beyond its power, so that it might destroy the nation of a wicked land.
verses.16:20: Instead of these things, You nourished Your people with the food of angels, and provided for them prepared bread from heaven without labor, having every delight in itself and the pleasantness of every taste.
verses.16:21: For Your substance showed Your sweetness, which You have toward children; and serving the will of each one, it was turned into whatever each one wished.
verses.16:22: Snow and ice, however, endured the force of fire and did not melt, so that they might know that fire, burning in hail and flashing in rain, was destroying the fruits of the enemies;
verses.16:23: yet this fire again, so that the righteous might be nourished, forgot even its own power.
verses.16:24: For creation, serving You, the Maker, blazes up into torment against the unrighteous, and becomes gentler to do good on behalf of those who trust in You.
verses.16:25: Because of this, at that time also, transformed into all things, it served Your grace, the nourisher of all, according to the will of those who asked of You,
verses.16:26: so that Your children whom You loved, Lord, might know that it is not the fruits of growth that feed people, but Your word preserves those who believe in You.
verses.16:27: For what could not be destroyed by fire immediately melted when warmed by a slight ray of the sun,
verses.16:28: so that it might be known to all that it is necessary to anticipate the sun to bless You, and to worship You at the rising of the light.
verses.16:29: For the hope of the ungrateful will melt away like winter ice, and will perish like useless water.
verses.17:1: For great are Your judgments, Lord, and indescribable are Your words; because of this, undisciplined souls went astray.
verses.17:2: For while the wicked were persuaded that they could rule over the holy nation, shackled with bonds of darkness and a long night, shut in under roofs, they lay as fugitives from perpetual providence.
verses.17:3: And while they thought they were hidden in dark sins, they were scattered under a gloomy veil of forgetfulness, horribly terrified and troubled with extreme astonishment.
verses.17:4: For not even the cave that held them kept them without fear, since a descending sound troubled them, and gloomy figures appearing to them brought them terror.
verses.17:5: And indeed no force of fire could provide them light, nor could the bright flames of the stars illuminate that horrible night.
verses.17:6: Yet a sudden fire appeared to them, full of fear; and struck with fear of that appearance which was not seen, they judged the things that were seen to be worse.
verses.17:7: And the mockeries of the magical craft were put down, and there was a rebuke with disgrace for the glory of wisdom.
verses.17:8: For those who promised that they would drive out fears and troubles from a languishing soul, these languished with mockery, full of fear.
verses.17:9: For even if nothing from the monsters troubled them, shaken by the passing of animals and the hissing of serpents, trembling they were perishing, even denying that they saw the air, which no one could in any way escape.
verses.17:10: For since wickedness is timid, it gives testimony of condemnation; for it always presumes harsh things, troubled by conscience.
verses.17:11: For fear is nothing except a betrayal of the aids of thought.
verses.17:12: And while expectation from within is less, it reckons greater the ignorance of that cause from which it brings torment.
verses.17:13: But those who were sleeping the same sleep through a truly powerless night that came upon them both from the lowest and from the highest regions of the underworld,
verses.17:14: were sometimes driven by fear of monsters, and sometimes fainted through the surrender of the soul; for a sudden and unexpected fear had come upon them.
verses.17:15: Then, if anyone of them had fallen down, he was kept shut up in a prison without iron.
verses.17:16: For if anyone was a farmer, or a shepherd, or a worker at the labors of the field, and had been overtaken, he endured an inescapable necessity.
verses.17:17: For with one chain of darkness they were all bound together. Whether a whistling wind, or a pleasant sound of birds among dense branches of trees, or the force of water rushing down fiercely,
verses.17:18: or the mighty sound of rocks hurled down, or the unseen running of playing animals, or the mighty voice of bellowing beasts, or an echo resounding from the highest mountains: they made them faint from fear.
verses.17:19: For the whole world was illuminated with bright light, and was occupied with unhindered works.
verses.17:20: Over them alone, however, a heavy night had been laid, an image of the darkness that was about to come upon them; therefore they themselves were heavier to themselves than the darkness.
verses.18:1: For Your holy ones, however, there was very great light; and indeed they heard their voice, yet they did not see their form. And because they themselves also had not suffered the same things, they magnified You;
verses.18:2: and those who had previously been harmed, because they were not being harmed, gave thanks, and asked for the gift that there might be a difference.
verses.18:3: For this reason they had a burning pillar of fire as a guide for an unknown way, and You provided a sun without harm for a good sojourn.
verses.18:4: They indeed deserved to be deprived of light and to suffer the prison of darkness, those who kept Your sons confined, through whom the uncorrupted light of the law was beginning to be given to the world.
verses.18:5: When they planned to kill the infants of the righteous, and one son was exposed and delivered, for their rebuke You took away a multitude of sons, and destroyed them together in mighty water.
verses.18:6: For that night was known beforehand by our fathers, so that, truly knowing which oaths they had trusted, they might be more steadfast in spirit.
verses.18:7: Now the safety of the righteous indeed, but the destruction of the unrighteous, was awaited by Your people.
verses.18:8: For just as You harmed the adversaries, so also, calling us forth, You magnified us.
verses.18:9: For in secret the righteous children of the good were offering sacrifice, and in harmony they established the law of righteousness, that the righteous would alike receive both good and evil, already singing the praises of the fathers.
verses.18:10: But the discordant voice of the enemies resounded, and a tearful lamentation for the mourned infants was heard.
verses.18:11: And with a similar punishment the slave was afflicted along with the master, and the common man suffered things similar to the king's.
verses.18:12: Therefore all alike, under one name of death, had innumerable dead; for the living were not even sufficient to bury them, since in one moment that which was their nobler generation was destroyed.
verses.18:13: For not believing regarding all things because of sorceries, then indeed for the first time, when the destruction of the firstborn occurred, they acknowledged them to be the people of God.
verses.18:14: For while tranquil silence encompassed all things, and night in its course held the middle of its journey,
verses.18:15: Your all-powerful word sprang forth out of heaven, from the royal thrones, a stern warrior into the middle of the land of destruction,
verses.18:16: a sharp sword carrying Your unfeigned command, and standing, filled all things with death, and reached all the way to heaven while standing on the earth.
verses.18:17: Then immediately visions of evil dreams troubled them, and unexpected fears came upon them.
verses.18:18: And one thrown down half-dead here, another there, declared the cause of death on account of which he was dying.
verses.18:19: For the visions that troubled them forewarned of these things, so that they would not perish ignorant of why they were suffering evils.
verses.18:20: Then, however, the trial of death touched the righteous as well, and a commotion of the multitude took place in the wilderness; yet Your wrath did not remain for long.
verses.18:21: For a man without reproach, speeding to intercede for the peoples, bringing forward the shield of his service, presenting prayer and intercession through incense, withstood the wrath and put an end to the distress, showing that he is Your servant.
verses.18:22: Yet he overcame the crowds not by strength of body nor by the power of arms, but by a word he subdued the one who was afflicting him, recalling the oaths of the forefathers and the covenant.
verses.18:23: For when the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another, he stood between, and cut off the onslaught, and divided that way which led to the living.
verses.18:24: For on the full-length robe that he wore was the whole world, and the great deeds of the forefathers were engraved on the four rows of stones, and Your majesty was engraved on the diadem of his head.
verses.18:25: To these things, however, the one who was destroying yielded, and these he dreaded; for the trial of wrath alone was sufficient.
verses.19:1: Upon the ungodly, however, wrath came without mercy until the very end. For He also knew beforehand the things to come for them:
verses.19:2: that after they themselves had permitted them to leave, and had sent them forth with great urgency, they would pursue them, driven by regret.
verses.19:3: For while still having mourning in hand, and lamenting at the tombs of the dead, they took to themselves another thought of ignorance; and those whom they had cast out with pleas, these they pursued as fugitives.
verses.19:4: For a deserved necessity was leading them to this end, and they were losing the remembrance of these things that had happened, so that punishment might fill up what was lacking to the torments,
verses.19:5: and Your people indeed might pass through wonderfully, whereas they might find a new death.
verses.19:6: For the whole creation was being refashioned from the beginning according to its own kind, serving Your commands, so that Your children might be kept unharmed.
verses.19:7: For the cloud overshadowed their camp, and out of the water that was before, dry land appeared, and in the Red Sea a way without hindrance, and a sprouting plain out of the vast deep,
verses.19:8: through which the whole nation that was sheltered by Your hand passed, seeing Your wonders and portents.
verses.19:9: For like horses they fed on food, and like lambs they exulted, magnifying You, Lord, who delivered them.
verses.19:10: For they were still mindful of those things that had taken place during their sojourn: how instead of the generation of animals the earth brought forth flies, and instead of fish the river disgorged a multitude of frogs.
verses.19:11: And finally they saw a new creation of birds, when, led by craving, they asked for foods of feasting.
verses.19:12: For in consolation of desire, quail came up for them from the sea; and afflictions came upon the sinners, not without those signs that had occurred beforehand through the force of thunderbolts, for they suffered justly according to their own wicked deeds.
verses.19:13: For in fact they established a more detestable inhospitality: some indeed did not receive unknown strangers, while others reduced good guests to slavery.
verses.19:15: And not only these things, but there was also a certain other regard for them, since they received foreigners unwillingly.
verses.19:16: But they who with gladness received those who had enjoyed the same rights afflicted them with most cruel pains.
verses.19:17: And they were struck with blindness, just as those at the doors of the righteous one, when, covered with sudden darkness, each one searched for the passage of his own door.
verses.19:18: For while the elements are changed into one another, just as on a musical instrument the sound of the quality is altered, still all keep their own sound, by which it can be judged with certainty from the sight itself.
verses.19:19: For land creatures were changed into aquatic ones, and whatever things were swimming crossed over onto the land.
verses.19:20: Fire prevailed in water beyond its own strength, and water forgot its quenching nature.
verses.19:21: Flames, on the contrary, did not injure the flesh of perishable animals walking among them, nor did they melt that good food, which was easily melted like ice. For in all things You magnified Your people, Lord, and honored them, and did not despise them, standing by them at every time and in every place.

notes.1:5: Latin corripietur a superveniente iniquitate is a difficult passive rendering of Greek elenchthesetai, literally meaning "will be checked/rebuked by approaching iniquity," expressing that the Spirit withdraws or is offended when iniquity comes near.
notes.1:14: Vulgate sanabiles fecit nationes ("made the nations healable") is a distinctive Old Latin/Vulgate reading, whereas the Greek text reads "the generative creatures [or generations] of the world are wholesome."
notes.1:16: Latin feminine illam ("it") and amicam ("a friend") refer back to mortem ("death," feminine in Latin) in 1:12-13 rather than to justitia ("righteousness") in the parenthetical 1:15.
notes.2:2: Vulgate ex nihilo ("out of nothing") is distinctive compared with the Greek autoschedios ("by chance"); likewise sermo ... ad commovendum cor ("speech ... to stir our heart") reflects an Old Latin rendering of Greek logos ("reason") and en kinesei kardias ("in the beating of our heart").
notes.2:3: The Latin places "and our life will pass away like the trace of a cloud ... weighed down by its heat" in verse 3, whereas the Greek has it in verse 4, after the statement about our name.
notes.2:13: Vulgate filium Dei ("son of God") differs from the Greek paida kyriou ("servant/child of the Lord"), a distinctive Latin wording repeated with verus filius Dei in 2:18.
notes.2:23: Vulgate ad imaginem similitudinis suae ("in the image of His own likeness") preserves an Old Latin reading reflecting the Greek variant idiotetos ("own nature") rather than the standard Septuagint aidiotetos ("eternity").
notes.2:24: Vulgate imitantur autem illum ("imitate him [the devil]") is a well-known Vulgate-distinct reading contrasting with the Greek peirazousin de auton ("experience it [death]"); this verse also combines traditional 2:24-25 in the Clementine Vulgate.
notes.3:1: Vulgate tormentum mortis ("the torment of death") adds mortis ("of death"), which is absent from the standard Greek Septuagint.
notes.3:6: The Vulgate places et in tempore erit respectus illorum ("and in time there will be regard for them") as an independent clause at the end of 3:6, whereas the Greek joins "in the time of their visitation" to the opening of 3:7; respectus ("regard") renders Greek episkope ("visitation"), as in 2:20.
notes.3:9: Vulgate donum et pax ("gift and peace") differs from the standard Greek reading charis kai eleos ("grace and mercy").
notes.3:18: Latin in die agnitionis ("in the day of recognition") renders Greek diagnoseos ("decision/examination"), referring to the day of divine judgment.
notes.4:1: Vulgate-distinct reading: casta generatio, cum claritate ("a chaste generation with splendor") diverges sharply from the Greek Septuagint ("Better is childlessness with virtue").
notes.4:6: Literally "from unlawful sleeps" (ex iniquis somnis), an idiom referring to illicit sexual unions.
notes.4:14: Vulgate-distinct syntax: properavit educere illum makes God ("He") the subject who hurried to bring the righteous man out, whereas the Greek has his soul hurrying out of wickedness; verse 15 also adds Dei ("of God") and reverses the order of "holy ones" and "chosen ones."
notes.4:19: Vulgate-distinct readings: decidentes ("falling down") renders the Greek noun for "corpse/fall" as a participle, and inflatos sine voce ("puffed up without a voice") diverges from the Greek ("speechless, headlong").
notes.5:6: Vulgate-distinct reading: Latin adds intelligentiæ ("of understanding") to "the sun," and in 5:7 reads lassati sumus ("we grew weary") where the Greek has "we had our fill."
notes.5:13: Vulgate-distinct clause: Talia dixerunt in inferno hi qui peccaverunt ("Such things those who sinned spoke in the underworld") is a Vulgate transition not present in the standard Greek text.
notes.5:14: Vulgate-distinct reading: spuma gracilis ("thin foam") contrasts with the Greek Septuagint ("thin frost").
notes.5:17: Vulgate-distinct syntax: zelus illius ("His zeal") is the nominative subject of Accipiet ("will take up"), whereas the Greek treats "His zeal" as an accusative in apposition to "full armor."
notes.5:22: Vulgate-distinct reading: a petrosa ira plenæ ... grandines ("from stony wrath, full hailstones") reflects the Clementine Latin wording, whereas the Greek reads "from a catapult, hailstones full of wrath."
notes.6:1: Vulgate-distinct addition: the opening proverb Melior est sapientia quam vires, et vir prudens quam fortis ("Wisdom is better than strength, and a prudent man than a strong one") appears in the Clementine Vulgate but not in the standard Greek Septuagint.
notes.6:7: Vulgate-distinct readings: Latin reads Deus ("God") instead of the Greek "Master of all," renders "will not shrink from" literally as subtrahet ("will not exempt"), and contains the pleonastic double genitive ejus cujusquam ("anyone's").
notes.6:8: Vulgate-distinct reading: cruciatio ("torment") diverges from the Greek Septuagint ("scrutiny/examination").
notes.6:21: Vulgate-distinct addition: the closing exhortation diligite lumen sapientiæ, omnes qui præestis populis ("love the light of wisdom, all you who rule over peoples") is a Vulgate expansion absent from the main Greek text, as is perpetuum ("everlasting") in 6:20.
notes.7:11: Latin honestas (also in 7:13 and 8:18), ordinarily meaning honor or dignity, carries the Late Latin sense of wealth or honorable abundance here, rendering Greek ploutos.
notes.7:15: The Vulgate uses the past indicative dedit ("has granted") rather than the optative wish ("may God grant") found in the Greek Septuagint.
notes.7:21: Latin improvisa ("unforeseen") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek Septuagint has emphane ("manifest").
notes.7:23: The Vulgate renders intelligibilis, mundus, subtilis in the nominative singular describing the spirit of wisdom itself and uses capiat ("encompasses"), whereas the Greek uses genitive plurals modifying "all spirits" with a verb meaning "penetrates through."
notes.7:27: Latin per nationes ("through the nations") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek Septuagint has kata geneas ("in every generation").
notes.8:7: Latin virtus is used here both in the plural for "virtues" generally and in the singular at the end of the list for the fourth cardinal virtue of "fortitude" (rendering Greek andreia, courage).
notes.8:8: Latin argumentorum ("arguments") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek Septuagint has ainigmaton ("riddles").
notes.8:11: The final clause et facies principum mirabuntur me ("and the faces of princes will marvel at me") is a Vulgate-distinct addition absent from standard Greek Septuagint manuscripts.
notes.8:20: Latin cum essem magis bonus literally reads "since I was more good" (or "rather good"), rendering a debated Greek clause (mallon de agathos on, "or rather, being good") often discussed regarding the goodness of the soul and its union with the body.
notes.8:21: Latin continens ("self-controlled" or "continent") reflects a distinctly Vulgate reading of Greek enkrates, which in context can also mean "gaining possession" of wisdom.
notes.9:4: Both here (sedium tuarum) and in 9:12 (sedium patris mei), the Vulgate preserves the plural "thrones" (a majestic plural matching Greek thronon), whereas 9:10 uses the singular sede.
notes.9:10: Latin magnitudinis tuae ("of Your greatness") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek Septuagint has doxes sou ("of Your glory"); similarly, 9:11 reads potentia ("power") where Greek has doxe ("glory").
notes.9:16: Latin in prospectu ("in view") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Greek Septuagint has en chersin ("in our hands" or "close at hand").
notes.9:18: Latin sanati sunt ("were healed") and the concluding phrase quicumque placuerunt tibi, Domine, a principio ("all who pleased You, Lord, from the beginning") are Vulgate-distinct readings compared with the shorter Greek Septuagint text ("by wisdom they were saved").
notes.10:1: Vulgate a Deo patre orbis terrarum places patre in the ablative in apposition to Deo ("by God, the Father of the world"), whereas the Greek has the accusative "the first-formed father of the world," referring to Adam.
notes.10:5: Vulgate cum se nationes contulissent means "when the nations had gathered together," differing from the Greek "when the nations were confused." In the final clause, in filii misericordia refers to Abraham remaining steadfast amid compassion for his son Isaac.
notes.10:7: Vulgate figmentum salis literally means "a figure of salt" (something fashioned of salt, where Greek has "pillar of salt"), and incredibilis is used in its ecclesiastical Latin active sense of "unbelieving."
notes.10:12: Vulgate reads a seductoribus ("from deceivers," where Greek has "from those lying in ambush") and sapientia ("wisdom," where Greek has "godliness").
notes.10:19: Vulgate ab altitudine inferorum eduxit illos ("from the depth of the underworld she brought them up") differs from the Greek "cast them up from the depth of the abyss," allowing illos to evoke both the drowned enemies washed ashore for despoiling and Israel's rescue from the depths.
notes.11:5: The Vulgate includes the expanded clause a defectione potus sui, et in eis cum abundarent filii Israel laetati sunt ("from the lack of their drink, and in which the sons of Israel rejoiced when they had abundance"), which is absent from the Greek text.
notes.11:6: Vulgate specifies humanum sanguinem ("human blood"), whereas the Greek reads "foul blood."
notes.11:7: Vulgate Qui cum minuerentur ("While they were diminished") reflects a shift in pronoun reference between Egypt's punishment for the killed infants and God's unexpected gift of water to Israel; in 11:8 the Vulgate also adds tuos exaltares ("how You exalted Your own"), absent from the Greek.
notes.11:13: Vulgate bene secum agi uses the reflexive secum loosely in indirect discourse to refer to Israel's well-being (as in 11:5), and adds admirantes in finem exitus ("marveling at the end of the outcome"), which is absent from the Greek.
notes.11:17: Vulgate reads ex materia invisa ("out of unseen matter"), differing from the Greek "out of formless matter"; similarly in 11:20 the Vulgate has ab ipsis factis suis ("by their very own deeds") where the Greek has "by Justice."
notes.12:1: The Vulgate reads "good and sweet, Lord, is Your Spirit" (bonus et suavis est, Domine, spiritus tuus), whereas the Greek Septuagint has "your incorruptible spirit."
notes.12:5: The Vulgate "from the midst of Your mystery" (a medio sacramento tuo, lit. "sacrament/mystery") diverges from the Greek Septuagint, which refers to initiates from the midst of a cultic band.
notes.12:6: The Vulgate "authors" (auctores) translates Greek authentas, which in later Greek means "murderers" or "those who kill with their own hands."
notes.12:7: The Vulgate uses the plural verb "they might receive" (perciperent) and "sojourn" (peregrinationem), whereas the Greek Septuagint has a singular verb with "the land" as subject receiving a "colony."
notes.12:17: The Vulgate reads "of those who do not know You" (horum qui te nesciunt), contrasting with the Greek Septuagint ("among those who know [You]").
notes.12:18: The Vulgate "with great reverence" (cum magna reverentia) differs from the Greek Septuagint ("with great forbearance/sparing").
notes.13:2: The Vulgate explicitly names "the sun and the moon" (solem et lunam) and "immense water" (nimiam aquam), where the Greek Septuagint has "luminaries of heaven" and "violent water."
notes.13:5: The Vulgate "recognizably" (cognoscibiliter, lit. "in a knowable way") and "of beauty and of creation" (speciei et creaturae) correspond to the Greek Septuagint "by analogy" and "greatness and beauty of created things."
notes.13:11: The Vulgate reads "a straight piece of wood" (lignum rectum), contrasting with "crooked" in verse 13, whereas the Greek Septuagint has "an easily handled piece of wood."
notes.13:19: The Vulgate "the outcome of all things" (omnium rerum eventu) and "useless in all things" (in omnibus est inutilis) generalize the Greek Septuagint, which refers specifically to "success of hands" and "most feeble with its hands."
notes.14:2: The Clementine Vulgate includes 'sua' ('his'), making 'artifex' ('the craftsman') the subject and 'sapientia sua' ('by his wisdom') an ablative of means; the Greek Septuagint reads 'wisdom, the artisan, built it.'
notes.14:11: A Vulgate-distinct reading: 'non erit respectus' ('there will be no regard'), whereas the Greek Septuagint has no negative and refers to a 'visitation' (judgment) upon the idols of the nations.
notes.14:14: The Vulgate uses the nominative singular 'Supervacuitas ... hæc' with singular 'advenit' ('this futility ... came'), whereas the Greek Septuagint has a dative ('by the vainglory of men they entered').
notes.14:26: A Vulgate-distinct reading: 'Dei immemoratio' ('forgetfulness of God'), where the Greek Septuagint reads 'forgetfulness of gratitude' (or 'of favors').
notes.14:31: Latin 'juratorum' renders the Greek passive participle 'of the things sworn by' (the idols), though in Latin it could also be understood as 'of those who swear.'
notes.15:2: A Vulgate-distinct reading: 'et si non peccaverimus, scimus' ('and if we do not sin, we know'), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads 'but we will not sin, knowing that we are reckoned as Yours.'
notes.15:4: Latin 'umbra picturæ' ('shadow of a painting') reflects a literal rendering of Greek 'skiagraphon' ('painters,' literally 'shadow-painters'), and 'sculpta' ('carved') corresponds to Greek 'stained.'
notes.15:14: A Vulgate-distinct reading: 'supra modum animæ superbi' ('beyond measure, proud of soul,' or 'proud beyond the measure of a soul'), where the Greek Septuagint reads 'more wretched than the soul of an infant.'
notes.15:18: The Vulgate 'insensata enim comparata his, illis sunt deteriora' preserves two distinct demonstratives ('these' and 'those'), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads 'for compared in stupidity, they are worse than the others.'
notes.16:3: Vulgate 'propter ea quae illis ostensa et missa sunt' ("because of the things that were shown and sent to them") is a distinct Latin reading where the Greek has "because of the loathsomeness of the creatures sent upon them."
notes.16:11: Vulgate 'examinabantur' ("they were examined/tested") differs from the Greek reading, which means "they were stung/pricked."
notes.16:13: The Vulgate reads 'portas mortis' ("the gates of death") where the Greek has "the gates of Hades."
notes.16:19: Vulgate 'iniquae terrae nationem' ("the nation of a wicked land") renders Greek 'adikou ges genemata' ("the produce/crops of an unrighteous land"), taking 'genema' in the sense of offspring or nation.
notes.16:21: Latin 'Substantia' (rendering Greek 'hypostasis') literally means "substance" and can also carry the sense "sustenance," referring here to the manna.
notes.17:1: The Vulgate includes 'Domine' ("Lord") and 'verba tua' ("Your words"), whereas the Greek reads simply "Great are Your judgments and hard to explain."
notes.17:3: Vulgate 'cum admiratione nimia' ("with extreme astonishment") is a distinctly Latin reading where the Greek reads "terrified by apparitions."
notes.17:7: Latin 'appositi erant derisus' (literally "the mockeries were put/set down") corresponds to Greek 'empaigmata katekeito' ("the illusions lay prostrate/defeated").
notes.17:12: In this syntactically dense verse, Vulgate 'de qua tormentum praestat' ("from which it brings torment") corresponds to the Greek "the cause that produces the torment."
notes.17:13: Vulgate 'et ab infimis et ab altissimis inferis' ("both from the lowest and from the highest regions of the underworld") differs from the Greek, which reads "from the recesses of powerless Hades."
notes.18:1: The Vulgate reads magnificabant te ('they magnified You'), explicitly directing praise to God from the righteous, whereas the Greek has emakarizon ('they called them blessed'), referring to the Egyptians congratulating the Israelites.
notes.18:13: The Vulgate reads populum Dei esse ('to be the people of God'), whereas the Greek text reads 'the people to be God's son' (theou huion).
notes.18:16: In the Vulgate, gladius acutus ('a sharp sword') is nominative in apposition to the Word itself, whereas the Greek accusative makes the sword an object carried by the warrior.
notes.18:21: The Clementine Vulgate reads prosperans (lit. 'prospering/succeeding', a variant of properans, 'hastening', matching Greek speusas) and deprecari pro populis ('to intercede for the peoples') where Greek has 'fought as champion'.
notes.18:22: Vulgate turbas ('the crowds') reflects a Greek variant ochlon ('crowd/tumult') rather than cholon ('anger/wrath').
notes.19:13: Clementine Vulgate versification incorporates the clause numbered 19:14 in Greek editions into 19:13 (omitting verse number 14), and reads bonos hospites ('good guests') where Greek has 'guest-benefactors'.
notes.19:15: Vulgate respectus ('regard/consideration', rendering Greek episkope, 'visitation/scrutiny') and past-tense erat ('was') differ from the Greek future 'there will be a visitation for them'.
notes.19:18: Vulgate in organo qualitatis sonus immutatur ('on a musical instrument the sound of the quality is altered') is a distinct Latin rendering of the Greek comparison of harp notes changing the name of the rhythm while keeping their own tone.
notes.19:21: Clementine Vulgate merges Greek 19:22 into the end of verse 21, and reads bonam escam ('good food') where Greek has 'ambrosial/immortal food'.
